facts.fact: UNICEF reports that trained health workers at registration posts inside hospitals and health centres register births on a digital platform installed on a tablet, with a printer, and that since December 2024 nurses, social workers and midwives are authorised to register children under one; the article does not name the platform or say whether it is connected to a national register, and the date used is the article's.
facts.system: Birth registration posts in health services (digital platform on tablet)

facts.fact: UNICEF says digital registration is available in hospitals and health centres of three regions, Bissau, Tombali and Quinara, and gives no count of posts or total; it reports more than 20,000 children aged 0 to 7 registered between October 2024 and June 2025, 5,886 of them before age one.
facts.system: Birth registration posts in health services (digital platform on tablet)

facts.fact: UNICEF says the health-service registration posts run under its project Rumo ao Registo Universal de Nascimentos e Identidade Legal, financed by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation, which donated the tablets, computers, printers and motorbikes; no domestic funding is mentioned, and the date used is the article's.
facts.system: Birth registration posts in health services (digital platform on tablet)
